war: Tikang hito nga panahon, tungod kan Jose, ginpakaupay han Ginoo an panimalay han Ehiptohanon ngan an ngatanan niya nga mga butang nga nakada han iya balay ngan didto han iya kaumhan.

en: So he handed over everything he had to Joseph and didn’t pay attention to anything except the food he ate.
war: Igintubyan ni Potifar an ngatanan nga iya gintatag-iya ngadto han pagmangno ni Jose ngan waray na hiya manginlabot hin bisan ano gawas la han iya pagkaon.

en: Now Joseph was well-built and handsome.
war: Maupay an tindog han lawas ni Jose ngan gwapo hiya.

en: Some time later, his master’s wife became attracted to Joseph and said, “Sleep with me.”
war: Waray pag-iha nagtikang hin kaipa kan Jose an asawa han iya agaron ngan ginhangyo hi Jose nga makighilawas ha iya.

en: He refused and said to his master’s wife, “With me here, my master doesn’t pay attention to anything in his household; he’s put everything he has under my supervision.
war: Dinmiri hi Jose ngan nagsiring ha iya, “Tan-awa daw, diri nanginginlabot an akon agaron hin bisan ano dinhe ha balay kay aanhi man ako. Iginbutang ako niya nga tinaporan han ngatanan nga iya mga hiagi ug manggad.

en: No one is greater than I am in this household, and he hasn’t denied me anything except you, since you are his wife. How could I do this terrible thing and sin against God?”
war: May-ada ako sugad kadako nga gahom han iya gahom dinhe hini nga balay, ngan waray niya igdiri ha akon an bisan ano labot la ha imo. Sanglit uunanhon ko hin pakagbuhat hin sugad kamalaw-ay nga butang ngan pakasala kontra han Dyos?”

en: Every single day she tried to convince him, but he wouldn’t agree to sleep with her or even to be with her.
war: Bisan kon ginhangyo niya hi Jose adlaw-adlaw, waray gud umalagad hi Jose hin pakighilawas ha iya.

en: One day when Joseph arrived at the house to do his work, none of the household’s men were there.
war: Kundi usa ka adlaw, han pagsulod ni Jose han balay hin pagtuman han iya buruhaton, waray gud didto bisan usa han mga surugoon han balay.

en: She grabbed his garment, saying, “Lie down with me.” But he left his garment in her hands and ran outside.
war: Kinaptan niya hi Jose ha iya hilawig nga bado ngan ginsiring, “Tana, dirig ha akon.” Kundi kinmalagiw hi Jose ngan dinmalagan ha gawas nga binayaan an iya hilawig nga bado dida han kamot han babaye.

en: When she realized that he had left his garment in her hands and run outside,
war: Han paghikit-i han babaye nga binayaan ni Jose an iya hilawig nga bado ngan dinmalagan ha gawas han balay,

en: she summoned the men of her house and said to them, “Look, my husband brought us a Hebrew to ridicule us. He came to me to lie down with me, but I screamed.
war: gintawag niya an iya mga surugoon ngan ginsiring hira, “Tan-awa daw ini! Gintatamay kita hini nga Hebreohanon nga gindara han akon bana nganhi ha balay. Sinmulod hiya han akon kwarto ngan nagsari hin paglugos ha akon, kundi ginmoliat ako hin dako sugad han akon mahimo.

en: When he heard me raise my voice and scream, he left his garment with me and ran outside.”
war: Han pakabati la niya han akon paggoliat, binayaan niya an iya hilawig nga bado dinhe ha akon ngan dinmalagan hiya ha gawas.”

en: She kept his garment with her until Joseph’s master came home,
war: Ginhimos niya an hilawig nga bado ni Jose tubtob han pag-uli han agaron ni Jose.

en: and she told him the same thing: “The Hebrew slave whom you brought to us, to ridicule me, came to me;
war: Niyan ginsumatan niya an agaron han amo manta nga sumat: “Sinmulod han akon kwarto ngan ginpasipad-an ako hito nga oripon nga Hebreohanon nga imo gindara nganhi.

en: but when I raised my voice and screamed, he left his garment with me and ran outside.”
war: Kundi han paggoliat ko dinmalagan hiya ha gawas, nga binayaan niya an iya hilawig nga bado dinhe ha akon.”

en: When Joseph’s master heard the thing that his wife told him, “This is what your servant did to me,” he was incensed.
war: Napungot hin duro an agaron ni Jose

en: Joseph’s master took him and threw him in jail, the place where the king’s prisoners were held. While he was in jail,
war: ngan iginpadakop hiya ngan iginsulod ha prisohan han mga binilanggo han hadi, ngan didto nagpabilin hiya.

en: the LORD was with Joseph and remained loyal to him. He caused the jail’s commander to think highly of Joseph.
war: Kundi nakada kan Jose an Ginoo ngan ginbendisyonan hiya, sanglit nalipay ha iya an gwardya han prisohan.

en: The jail’s commander put all of the prisoners in the jail under Joseph’s supervision, and he was the one who determined everything that happened there.
war: Iginbutang niya hi Jose nga tinaporan han ngatanan nga mga priso ngan ginhimo hiya nga may kaakohan han ngatanan nga ginbubuhat didto han prisohan.

en: Some time later, both the wine steward and the baker for Egypt’s king offended their master, the king of Egypt.
war: Paglabay hin panahon nakatalapas han hadi han Ehipto an iya tinaporan han bino ngan an iya labaw nga parahimo hin tinapay.

en: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief wine steward and the chief baker,
war: Nasina hiya hini nga duha nga mga opisyal,

en: and he put them under arrest with the commander of the royal guard in the same jail where Joseph was imprisoned.
war: ngan ginpriso hira didto han balay han kapitan han gwardya, didto han amo manta nga dapit nga ginbutangan kan Jose.

en: The commander of the royal guard assigned Joseph to assist them. After they had been under arrest for some time,
war: Nag-iha hira didto han prisohan, ngan ginhimo han kapitan hi Jose nga ira surugoon.

en: both of them—the wine steward and the baker for Egypt’s king who were imprisoned in the jail—had dreams one night, and each man’s dream had its own meaning.
war: Usa ka gab-i didto han prisohan nag-inop an tinaporan han bino ngan an labaw nga parahimo han tinapay, ngan may-ada magkalain nga kahulogan an ira mga inop.

en: When Joseph met them in the morning, he saw that they were upset.
war: Han pagkadtoa ha ira ni Jose dida han aga, hinkit-an niya nga masulob-on hira.

en: He asked the officers of Pharaoh who were under arrest with him in his master’s house, “Why do you look so distressed today?”
war: Nagpakiana hiya ha ira, “Kay ano nga masulob-on kamo hin duro pagkit-on yana adlaw?”

en: They answered, “We’ve both had dreams, but there’s no one to interpret them.”
war: Binmaton hira, “Nag-inop an kada usa ha amon ngan waray gud dinhe tawo nga nakakagsaysay han kahulogan han mga inop.”

en: Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Describe your dreams to me.”
war: Nagsiring hi Jose, “An Dyos amo an nahatag hin kaaram hin paghubad hin mga inop. Sumati ako han iyo mga inop.”

en: The chief wine steward described his dream to Joseph: “In my dream there was a vine right in front of me,
war: Sanglit nagsiring an tinaporan han bino, “Dida han akon inop may-ada usa ka puno hin ubas ha akon atubangan

en: and on the vine were three branches. When it budded, its blossoms appeared, and its clusters ripened into grapes.
war: nga may-ada tulo nga mga sanga. Kahuman gud la panaringsing hini, nanmunga ini ngan nagkahihinog an mga ubas.

en: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, so I took the grapes, crushed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and put the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.”
war: Kinakaptan ko an kupa han hadi; sanglit kinuha ko an mga bunga han ubas ngan ginpuga ko ini ngadto han kupa, ngan iginhatag ko ini ha iya.”

en: Joseph said to him, “This is the dream’s interpretation: The three branches are three days.
war: Nagsiring hi Jose, “Amo ini an kahulogan hini: an tulo nga mga sanga amo an tulo ka adlaw.

en: After three days, Pharaoh will give you an audience and return you to your position. You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand, just the way things were before when you were his wine steward.
war: Tulo nala ka adlaw bubuhian ka an han hadi, pasasayloon ka, ngan igbabalik ka ngadto han imo katungdanan. Ighahatag mo ha iya an iya kupa sugad han imo ginbuhat hadto anay han ikaw pa an iya tinaporan han bino.

en: But please, remember me when you are doing well and be loyal to me. Put in a good word for me to Pharaoh, so he sets me free from this prison.
war: Kundi hinumdomi gad ako kon maghingaupay ka na, ngan malooy ka unta hin paghinabi ha akon ngadto han hadi ngan buligan ako hin paggawas dinhe hini nga prisohan.

en: I was stolen from the land of the Hebrews, and here too I’ve done nothing to be thrown into this dungeon.”
war: Ha tinuod gud, ginkawat la ako pagdad-a nganhi tikang han tuna han mga Hebreohanon, ngan bisan pa dinhe ha Ehipto waray ko ginbuhat nga bisan ano nga sadang pasikaran han akon kapriso.”

en: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favorable, he said to Joseph, “It was the same for me. In my dream, there were three baskets of white bread on my head.
war: Han pakakita han labaw nga parahimo han tinapay nga maupay an kahulogan han inop han tinaporan han bino, nagsiring hiya kan Jose, “Nag-inop liwat ako; nagtutukdo ako hin tulo nga mga basket nga surudlan hin tinapay.

en: In the basket on top there were baked goods for Pharaoh’s food, but birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.”
war: Didto han bawbaw nga basket nakadto an magkalainlain nga hinudno nga mga pagkaon nga para han hadi, ngan ginkikinaon ini han katamsihan.”

en: Joseph responded, “This is the dream’s interpretation: The three baskets are three days.
war: Binmaton hi Jose, “Amo ini an kahulogan: an tulo nga mga basket amo an tulo ka adlaw.

en: After three days, Pharaoh will give you an audience and will hang you from a tree where birds will peck your flesh from you.”
war: Tulo nala ka adlaw bubuhian ka na han hadi—ngan papupugotan ka niya! Niyan iya pagbibitayon an imo lawas dida hin usa nga palo ngan pangangaonon han katamsihan an imo unod.”

en: The third day was Pharaoh’s birthday, and he gave a party for all of his servants. Before all of his servants, he gave an audience to the chief wine steward and the chief baker.
war: Paglabay hin tulo ka adlaw, dida han kaadlawan han hadi naghatag hiya hin usa nga kombite para han ngatanan niya nga mga opisyal. Ginbuhian niya an iya tinaporan han bino ngan an iya lagaw nga parahimo hin tinapay ngan gindara hira ha atubangan han iya mga opisyal.

en: He returned the chief wine steward to his position, and he placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.
war: Iginbalik niya an tinaporan han bino ngadto han iya una nga katungdanan,

en: But the chief baker he hanged, just as Joseph had said would happen when he interpreted their dreams for them.
war: kundi iya iginpapatay an labaw nga parahimo hin tinapay. Natuman an ngatanan sugad gud han iginsiring ni Jose.

en: Two years later, Pharaoh dreamed that he was standing near the Nile.
war: Paglabay hin duha ka tuig nag-inop an hadi han Ehipto nga natukdaw hiya ha ligid han Salog han Nilo.

en: In front of him, seven healthy-looking, fattened cows climbed up out of the Nile and grazed on the reeds.
war: Nanagka tikang han salog in pito nga mga baka nga magtambok ngan maglibsog ngan nagtikang ini panabsab han mga banwa.

en: Just then, seven other cows, terrible-looking and scrawny, climbed up out of the Nile after them and stood beside them on the bank of the Nile.
war: Niyan nanagka liwat in pito nga lain nga mga baka nga maggasaay ngan nanhahataw an mga tulan hini. Tinmindog hira ha sapit han una nga mga baka dida han pangpang han salog,

en: The terrible-looking, scrawny cows devoured the seven healthy-looking, fattened cows. Then Pharaoh woke up.
war: ngan pinangaon han pito nga maggasaay nga mga baka an pito nga magtambok nga mga baka. Onina nagmata an hadi.

en: He went back to sleep and had a second dream, in which seven ears of grain, full and healthy, grew on a single stalk.
war: Nahingaturog liwat hiya ngan nag-inop hin ikaduha. Nagbuswak dida hin usa la nga lawas hin trigo in pito nga mga uhay nga maglibsog ngan magtimgas.

en: Just then, seven ears of grain, scrawny and scorched by the east wind, sprouted after them,
war: Niyan binmuswak liwat in pito nga lain nga mga uhay hin trigo nga mga kuyapi ngan mga apa tungod han mapaso nga hangin,

en: and the scrawny ears swallowed up the full and well-formed ears. Then Pharaoh woke up and realized it was a dream.
war: ngan ginlam-oy han kuyapi ngan apa nga mga uhay an pito nga mga uhay nga magtimgas. Nagmata an hadi ngan nakasabot hiya nga usa la adto nga inop.

en: In the morning, he was disturbed and summoned all of Egypt’s religious experts and all of its advisors. Pharaoh described his dreams to them, but they couldn’t interpret them for Pharaoh.
war: Han pagkaaga na naguol hiya, sanglit ginpasogoan niya an ngatanan nga mga salamangkero ngan mga makinaadmananon nga mga tawo han Ehipto. Iya ginsumatan hira han iya mga inop, kundi waray gud usa nga nakagsaysay han iya mga inop.

en: Then the chief wine steward spoke to Pharaoh: “Today I’ve just remembered my mistake.
war: Niyan nagsiring han hadi an tinaporan han bino, “Kinahanglan magtug-an ako yana nga adlaw nga nakasayop ako.

en: Pharaoh was angry with his servants and put me and the chief baker under arrest with the commander of the royal guard.
war: Hadto, nasinahan mo an labaw nga parahimo hin tinapay ngan hi ako, ngan iginpapriso mo kami didto han balay han kapitan han gwardya.

en: We both dreamed one night, he and I, and each of our dreams had its own interpretation.
war: Usa ka gab-i nag-inop an kada usa ha amon ngan may-ada magkalain nga mga kahulogan an mga inop.

en: A young Hebrew man, a servant of the commander of the royal guard, was with us. We described our dreams to him, and he interpreted our dreams for us, giving us an interpretation for each dream.
war: Nakadto upod ha amon in usa nga batan-on nga Hebreohanon, nga oripon han kapitan han gwardya. Ginsumatan hiya namon han amon mga inop ngan iya ginhubad ini para ha amon.

en: His interpretations came true exactly: Pharaoh restored me to my position but hanged him.”
war: Natuman ini sumala gud han iya iginsiring: iginbalik mo ako ngadto han akon katungdanan, kundi ginpapatay mo an labaw nga parahimo hin tinapay.”

en: So Pharaoh summoned Joseph, and they quickly brought him from the dungeon. He shaved, changed clothes, and appeared before Pharaoh.
war: Ginpasugoan han hadi hi Jose, ngan gindara hiya hin kadagmitan tikang han prisohan. Katapos niya magbarbas ngan magliwan, kinmadto hiya ha atubangan han hadi.

en: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I had a dream, but no one could interpret it. Then I heard that when you hear a dream, you can interpret it.”
war: Nagsiring ha iya an hadi, “Nag-inop ako ngan waray gud tawo nga nakakaghubad hini. Ginsumatan ako nga nakakahubad ka hin mga inop.”

en: Joseph answered Pharaoh, “It’s not me. God will give Pharaoh a favorable response.”
war: Binmaton hi Jose, “Diri ako makakahimo, Harangdon nga Hadi, kundi mahatag an Dyos hin maupay nga paghubad.”

en: So Pharaoh said to Joseph, “In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile.
war: 17-18 Nagsiring an hadi, “Nag-inop ako nga natukdaw ako didto han pangpang han Nilo. Nanagka tikang ha salog in pito nga mga baka nga magtambok ngan maglibsog ngan nagtikang ini hin panabsab han kabanwaan.

en: In front of me, seven fattened, stout cows climbed up out of the Nile and grazed on the reeds.
war: Niyan nanagka liwat in lain nga pito nga mga baka nga maggasaay ngan nanhahataw an ira mga tul-an. Amo hira an gigagasai nga mga baka nga akon hinkit-an ha bug-os nga tuna han Ehipto.

en: Just then, seven other cows, weak and frail and thin, climbed up after them. I’ve never seen such awful cows in all the land of Egypt.
war: Kinaon han maggasaay nga mga baka an magtambok nga mga baka,

en: Then the thin, frail cows devoured the first seven, fattened cows.
war: kundi waray gud nahibaro hini, kay maggasa man la gihapon hira pagkit-on sugad han una. Niyan nagmata ako.

en: But after they swallowed them whole, no one would have known it. They looked just as bad as they had before. Then I woke up.
war: Nag-inop liwat ako nga hinkit-an ko in pito nga mga uhay hin trigo nga maglibsog ngan magtimgas nga nanbuswak dida hin usa la nga tanom.

en: I went to sleep again and saw in my dream seven full and healthy ears of grain growing on one stalk.
war: Niyan binmuswak in pito nga mga uhay hin trigo nga mga kuyapi ngan apa tungod han mapaso nga hangin.

en: Just then, seven hard and thin ears of grain, scorched by the east wind, sprouted after them,
war: Ginlam-oy han kuyapi nga mga uhay an mga magtimgas. Iginsumat ko ini nga mga inop ngadto han mga salamangkero, kundi waray gud usa ha ira nga nakagsaysay han mga inop.”

en: and the thin ears swallowed up the healthy ears. I told the religious experts, but they couldn’t explain it to me.”
war: Nagsiring hi Jose han hadi, “Waray kalainan an kahulogan han duha nga mga inop; iginsumat ha imo han Dyos kon ano an iya pagbubuhaton.

en: Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Pharaoh has actually had one dream. God has announced to Pharaoh what he is about to do.
war: Pito ka tuig hin kahuraan an kahulogan han pito nga magtambok nga mga baka, ngan an pito nga magtimgas nga mga uhay hin trigo.

en: The seven healthy cows are seven years, and the seven healthy ears of grain are seven years. It’s actually one dream.
war: Pito ka tuig nga gutom an pito nga maggasaay nga mga baka nga inmabot sunod hini ngan an pito nga kuyapi ngan apa nga mga uhay hin trigo.

en: The seven thin and frail cows, climbing up after them, are seven years. The seven thin ears of grain, scorched by the east wind, are seven years of famine.
war: Amo gud ini sumala han akon iginsumat ha imo—iginpakita ha imo han Dyos kon ano an iya pagbubuhaton.

en: It’s just as I told Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.
war: Magkakamay-ada pito ka tuig nga kahuraan ha bug-os nga tuna han Ehipto.

en: Seven years of great abundance are now coming throughout the entire land of Egypt.
war: Katapos hito, magkakamay-ada pito ka tuig nga gutom, ngan hingangalimtan an ngatanan nga mag-upay nga katuigan, kay pinaagi han gutom mawawarayan gud an bug-os nga tuna.

en: After them, seven years of famine will appear, and all of the abundance in the land of Egypt will be forgotten. The famine will devastate the land.
war: Hingangalimtan gud an panahon hin kahuraan kay makalilisang an masunod nga gutom.

en: No one will remember the abundance in the land because the famine that follows will be so very severe.
war: An pagduhaa hini nga imo inop, nangangahulogan nga ginlarang na gud ini han Dyos, ngan nga pagtutumanon manta ini niya ha diri na maiha.

en: The dream occurred to Pharaoh twice because God has determined to do it, and God will make it happen soon.
war: “Yana kinahanglan magpili ka hin tawo nga makinaadmananon ngan maaram ngan igbutang mo hiya nga tinaporan han nasod.

en: “Now Pharaoh should find an intelligent, wise man and give him authority over the land of Egypt.
war: Kinahanglan magtudlok ka liwat hin iba nga mga opisyal nga magdudumara han nasod nga makuhaa an ika-lima ka bahin han mga abot, sulod han pito ka tuig nga kahuraan.

en: Then Pharaoh should appoint administrators over the land and take one-fifth of all the produce of the land of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
war: Papagtiroka hira han ngatanan nga pagkaon sulod han hura nga katuigan nga tiarabot, ngan tagi hira hin pagburot-an hin paghimos han mga trigo didto han mga syudad, ngan pagbantay hini.

en: During the good years that are coming, they should collect all such food and store the grain under Pharaoh’s control, protecting the food in the cities.
war: Magigin andam ini nga pagkaon para han nasod sulod han pito ka tuig nga gutom nga tiarabot dinhe ha Ehipto, basi diri gugutomon an mga tawo.”

en: This food will be reserved for the seven years of famine to follow in the land of Egypt so that the land won’t be ravaged by the famine.”
war: Gin-abuyonan han hadi ngan han iya mga opisyal ini nga larang,

en: This advice seemed wise to Pharaoh and all his servants,
war: ngan nagsiring ha ira an hadi, “Diri na gud kita makakaagi hin mauruupay nga tawo kay kan Jose nga usa nga tawo nga may espiritu han Dyos dida ha iya.”

en: and Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find a man with more God-given gifts than this one?”
war: Nagsiring an hadi kan Jose, “Iginpakita han Dyos ngada ha imo ini ngatanan, sanglit may-ada gud nimo darudako nga kinaadman ug kaaram kay han bisan hin-o.

en: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, no one is as intelligent and wise as you are.
war: Igbubutang ko ikaw nga tinaporan han akon nasod ngan magsusugot han imo mga sugo an ngatanan nga akon mga tawo. Mag-iikaduha ka gud ha akon hin kagamhanan.

en: You will be in charge of my kingdom, and all my people will obey your command. Only as the enthroned king will I be greater than you.”
war: Yana gintutudlok ko ikaw nga gobernador han bug-os nga Ehipto.”

en: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Know this: I’ve given you authority over the entire land of Egypt.”
war: Ginhulso han hadi an iya singsing nga pinatikan han hadianon nga silyo tikang han iya tudlo ngan iginsul-ot ini dida han tudlo ni Jose. Iya ginsul-otan hi Jose hin hilawig nga bado nga lino nga pino, ngan ginkwintasan hiya hin bulawan.

en: Pharaoh took his signet ring from his hand and put it on Joseph’s hand, he dressed him in linen clothes, and he put a gold necklace around his neck.
war: Iginhatag ha iya an ikaduha nga hadianon nga karuwahe nga ginsakyan ni Jose ngan nag-una ha iya an iya hadianon nga mga gwardya nga naggoliat, “Tagi hin lugar! Pagkaluhod kamo!” Sanglit gintudlok hi Jose nga gobernador han bug-os nga Ehipto.

en: He put Joseph on the chariot of his second-in-command, and everyone in front of him cried out, “Attention!” So Pharaoh installed him over the entire land of Egypt.
war: Nagsiring ha iya an hadi, “Amo ako an hadi—ngan waray tawo ha bug-os nga Ehipto nga makakagbuhat hin bisan ano, kon waray nimo pagtugot.”

en: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh; no one will do anything or go anywhere in all the land of Egypt without your permission.”
war: 45-46 Iginngaran niya kan Jose an Ehiptohanon nga ngaran nga Zafenat-panea, ngan iya gintagan hiya hin asawa nga hi Asenat nga anak ni Potifera nga usa nga padi didto han syudad han Heliopolis.

en: Pharaoh renamed Joseph, Zaphenath-paneah, and married him to Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera the priest of Heliopolis.
war: Treinta na an panuigon ni Jose han pagtikang niya hin pag-alagad ha hadi han Ehipto. Binayaan niya an palasyo han hadi ngan nagsudoy hiya han bug-os nga tuna.

en: Then Joseph assumed control of the land of Egypt.
war: Sulod han pito ka tuig nga kahuraan naghatag an tuna hin damo gud nga mga abot.

en: Joseph was 30 years old when he began to serve Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, when he left Pharaoh’s court and traveled through the entire land of Egypt.
war: Gintirok ni Jose an ngatanan ngan ginhimos ini didto han mga syudad. Didto han kada syudad gintirok niya an pagkaon tikang han kaumhan ha palibot hini.

en: During the seven years of abundance, the land produced plentifully.
war: May-ada damo hin duro nga mga liniso nga hinmunong nala hi Jose hin pagtinakos hini—pareho ini han baras ha baybayon.

en: He collected all of the food during the seven years of abundance in the land of Egypt, and stored the food in cities. In each city, he stored the food from the fields surrounding it.
war: Han waray pa aabot an mga tuig han gutom, nagkamay-ada hira Jose ug Asemat duha nga mga anak nga kalalaken-an.

en: Joseph amassed grain like the sand of the sea. There was so much that he stopped trying to measure it because it was beyond measuring.
war: Nagsiring hi Jose, “Ginpakalimot ako han Dyos han ngatanan ko nga mga pag-antos ngan han bug-os nga panimalay han akon amay”; sanglit ginngaranan niya nga Manases an iya suhag nga lalake.

en: Before the years of famine arrived, Asenath the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, gave birth to two sons for Joseph.
war: Nagsiring liwat hiya, “Gintagan ako han Dyos hin mga anak didto han tuna han akon kakurian”; sanglit ginngaranan niya nga Efraim an iya ikaduha nga anak nga lalake.

en: Joseph named the oldest son Manasseh, “because,” he said, “God has helped me forget all of my troubles and everyone in my father’s household.”
war: Natapos an pito ka tuig nga kahuraan nga ginpahimulosan han tuna han Ehipto,

en: He named the second Ephraim, “because,” he said, “God has given me children in the land where I’ve been treated harshly.”
war: ngan nagtikang an pito ka tuig nga gutom, sumala han iginsiring ni Jose. May-ada gutom didto han iba nga mga nasod, kundi may-ada pagkaon ha bug-os nga Ehipto.

en: The seven years of abundance in the land of Egypt came to an end,
war: Han pagtikang na hin paggutoma han mga Ehiptohanon, nagsangpit hira han hadi hin pangaro hin pagkaon. Sanglit iya ginpakadto hira kan Jose ngan iginpabuhat niya an kan Jose iginsiring ha ira.

en: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. The famine struck every country, but the entire land of Egypt had bread.
war: Nagtikagrabi na an gutom ngan nagsarang na ini ha bug-os nga nasod, sanglit ginbuksan ni Jose an ngatanan nga mga kamalig nga hirimosan ngan ginbaligyaan hin trigo an mga Ehiptohanon.

en: When the famine ravaged the entire land of Egypt and the people pleaded to Pharaoh for bread, Pharaoh said to all of the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. Do whatever he tells you.”
war: Inmabot ha Ehipto in mga tawo tikang ha bug-os nga kalibutan hin pagpalit hin trigo kan Jose, kay grabi na gud an gutom ha ngatanan nga mga dapit.

en: When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you staring blankly at each other?
war: Han paghibaro ni Jacob nga may-ada baligya nga trigo didto ha Ehipto, ginsiring niya an iya mga anak nga kalalaken-an, “Kay ano nga diri lugod kamo magmalahimo?

en: I’ve just heard that there’s grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us so that we can survive and not starve to death.”
war: Hinbatian ko nga may baligya nga trigo didto ha Ehipto; kadto ngan palit kamo basi diri kita mamatay hin gutom.”

en: So Joseph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain in Egypt.
war: Sanglit kinmadto an kan Jose napulo nga kabugtoan ha amay hin pagpalit hin trigo didto ha Ehipto,

en: However, Jacob didn’t send Joseph’s brother Benjamin along with his brothers because he thought something bad might happen to him.
war: kundi waray pagpaupda ha ira ni Jacob an tunay nga bugto ni Jose nga hi Benjamin, kay nahadlok hiya nga bangin may mahinabo ha iya.

en: Israel’s sons came to buy grain with others who also came since the famine had spread to the land of Canaan.
war: Nagkaabot an mga anak ni Jacob upod hin iba nga mga tawo hin pagpalit hin trigo, kay gutom na didto ha tuna han Canaan.

en: As for Joseph, he was the land’s governor, and he was the one selling grain to all the land’s people. When Joseph’s brothers arrived, they bowed down to him, their faces to the ground.
war: Nagbabaligya hi Jose, sugad nga gobernador han tuna han Ehipto, hin trigo ngadto han mga tawo nga tikang han bug-os nga kalibutan. Sanglit nagkaabot an kabugtoan ni Jose ngan hinmapa hira ha atubangan niya.

en: When Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he acted like he didn’t know them. He spoke to them with a harsh tone and said, “Where have you come from?”
war: Han paghikit-i ni Jose han iya kabugtoan, kinmilala hiya ha ira, kundi waray hiya magpakilala ha ira. Iya gin-isgan hira hin pagpakiana, “Diin kamo tikang?”

en: And they said, “From the land of Canaan to buy food.”
war: “Tikang kami ha Canaan ngan napalit kami hin pagkaon,” binmaton hira.

en: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they didn’t recognize him.
war: Kinmilala hi Jose han iya kabugtoan, kundi waray hira kumilala ha iya.

en: Joseph remembered the dreams he had dreamed about them, and said to them, “You are spies. You’ve come to look for the country’s weaknesses.”
war: Nahinumdom hiya han iya mga inop mahitungod ha ira, ngan nagsiring hiya, “Mga espiya kamo; kinmanhi kamo hin pag-inaw kon hain an maluya nga dapit han amon nasod.”

en: They said to him, “No, Master. Your servants have just come to buy food.
war: Binmaton hira, “Diri gad, ginoo. Kinmanhi kami sugad nga imo mga oripon, hin pagpalit hin pagkaon.

en: We are all sons of one man. We are honest men. Your servants aren’t spies.”
war: Magburugto kami ngatanan. Diri gad kami mga espiya, ginoo, tangkod kami nga mga tawo.”

en: He said to them, “No. You’ve come to look for the country’s weaknesses.”
war: Nagsiring ha ira hi Jose, “Diri! Kinmanhi kamo hin pag-inaw kon hain an maluya nga dapit han amon nasod.”

en: They said, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, but one is gone.”
war: Nagsiring hira, “Ginoo, dose kami ngatanan nga magburugto nga mga anak hin usa la ka tawo didto ha tuna han Canaan. Patay na an usa nga bugto, ngan upod han amon amay an gimamanghori.”

en: Joseph said to them, “It’s just as I’ve said to you. You are spies!
war: Binmaton hi Jose, “Sumala han akon iginsiring, mga espiya gud kamo.

en: But here is how to prove yourselves: As Pharaoh lives, you won’t leave here until your youngest brother arrives.
war: Amo ini an paagi hin pagsari ha iyo: nagsusumpa ako pinaagi han ngaran han hadi nga diri gud kamo mabaya dinhe kon diri kumanhi anay an iyo gimamanghori nga bugto.

en: Send one of you to get your brother, but the rest of you will stay in prison. We will find out if your words are true. If not, as Pharaoh lives, you are certainly spies.”
war: Kinahanglan kumadto in usa ha iyo hin pagkuha ha iyo. Pagbabantayan an mahibibilin ha iyo tubtob nga hisabtan an kamatuoran han iyo isinsiring. Kon diri, sugad nga buhi gud an hadi, mga espiya gud kamo.”

en: He put them all in prison for three days.
war: Katapos hito, iya ginpriso hira sulod hin tulo ka adlaw.

en: On the third day, Joseph said to them, “Do this and you will live, for I’m a God-fearing man.
war: Dida han ikatulo ka adlaw, nagsiring ha ira hi Jose, “Tawo ako nga may pagkahadlok han Dyos, ngan tatalwason ko an iyo mga kinabuhi, kundi may-ada niyo pagtutuman-on.

en: If you are honest men, let one of your brothers stay in prison, and the rest of you, go, take grain back to those in your households who are hungry.
war: Ha pagpakita nga mga tangkod kamo, magpapabilin in usa ha iyo didto han prisohan nga ginprisohan ha iyo; makakauli an iba ha iyo hin pagdara ngan han trigo nga iyo ginpalit para han iyo pinangagugutom nga mga panimalay.

en: But bring your youngest brother back to me so that your words will prove true and you won’t die.”
war: Ngan kinahanglan pagdad-on niyo nganhi ha akon an iyo gimamanghori nga bugto nga lalake. Magpapakita ini nga nagsumat kamo han kamatuoran, ngan diri ko kamo pamamatayon.”

en: So they prepared to do this.
war: Inmabuyon hira hini,

en: The brothers said to each other, “We are clearly guilty for what we did to our brother when we saw his life in danger and when he begged us for mercy, but we didn’t listen. That’s why we’re in this danger now.”
war: ngan naggipasiringsiring hira, “Tinuod nga nag-aantos na kita yana tungod han aton ginbuhat han aton bugto. Hinkit-an ta an dako niya nga kakurian han pakimalooy niya ha aton, kundi waray gud la kita mamati. Sanglit inmuntol ha aton yana ini nga kakurian.”

en: Reuben responded to them, “Didn’t I tell you, ‘Don’t do anything wrong to the boy’? But you wouldn’t listen. So now this is payback for his death.”
war: Nagsiring hi Ruben, “Ginsiring ko kamo nga diri ta paglabtan an bata, kundi waray man kamo bumali. Sanglit yana sinusuktan na kita tungod han iya kamatayon.”

en: They didn’t know that Joseph was listening to them because they were using an interpreter.
war: Nasayoran ni Jose an ira iginsiring, kundi waray hira makasabot, kay nakigkarukayakan hira ha iya pinaagi hin parahubad.

en: He stepped away from them and wept. When he returned, he spoke with them again. Then he took Simeon from them and tied him up in front of them.
war: Binayaan hira ni Jose ngan nagtangis hiya. Han pakahimo na liwat niya hin pagyakan binmalik hiya, ginkuha niya hi Simeon, ngan ginpagapos hiya ha atubangan nira.

en: Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, to put back each man’s silver into his own sack, and to give them provisions for their trip, and it was done.
war: Nagsugo hi Jose nga pun-on hin trigo an mga sako han iya kabugtoan, nga igbalik an kwarta han kada tawo ngadto han iya sako, ngan nga tagan hira hin pagkaon para han ira paglalaktan. Ginbuhat ini.

en: They loaded their grain onto their donkeys, and they set out.
war: Ginkargahan han kabugtoan an ira mga asno han trigo nga ira ginpalit, ngan nagkalakat hira.

en: When they stopped to spend the night, one of them opened his sack to feed his donkey, and he saw his silver at the top of his sack.
war: Didto han dapit nga ginpalabyan nira han gab-i, nag-abre han iya sako an usa ha ira hin pagtubong han iya asno, ngan hin-agian niya an iya kwarta dida han ganggang han iya sako.

en: He said to his brothers, “My silver’s been returned. It’s right here in my sack.” Their hearts stopped. Terrified, they said to each other, “What has God done to us?”
war: Gintawag ngan ginsiring niya an iya kabugtoan, “Igin-uli ha akon an akon kwarta! Aadi man ini han akon sako.” Pinangulba hira ngan naggiparupakiana hira tungod hin kahadlok, “Ano daw ini nga ginbuhat ha aton han Dyos?”

en: When they got back to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they described to him everything that had happened to them:
war: Han pag-abot nira ngadto kan Jacob nga ira amay didto ha Canaan, ira ginsumatan hiya han ngatanan nga nahinabo ha ira:

en: “The man, the country’s governor, spoke to us with a harsh tone and accused us of being spies in the country.
war: “Gin-isgan kami han gobernador han Ehipto ngan ginpasangilan kami nga mga espiya kontra han iya nasod.

en: We told him, ‘We’re honest men, not spies.
war: Binmaton kami, ‘Diri gad kami mga espiya, mga tangkod la kami nga mga tawo.

en: We are twelve brothers, all our father’s sons. One of us is gone, but the youngest is right now with our father in the land of Canaan.’
war: Dose kami ngatanan nga magburugto, nga mga anak hin usa la nga amay. Patay na an usa nga bugto ngan aadto pa ha Canaan an gimamanghori, upod han amon amay.’

en: The man, the country’s governor, told us, ‘This is how I will know you are honest men: Leave one of your brothers with me, take grain for those in your households who are hungry, and go.
war: Binmaton an tawo, ‘Amo ini an paagi nga hibabaroan ko kon mga tangkod manggud kamo nga mga tawo: mapabilin upod ha akon in usa ha iyo; malakat an iba ha iyo hin pagdara hin trigo para han iyo ginugutom nga mga panimalay.

en: But bring back your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies but honest men. I will give your brother back to you, and you may travel throughout the country.’”
war: Dad-a nganhi ha akon an iyo gimamanghori nga bugto. Niyan mahibabaroan ko nga diri kamo mga espiya, kundi tangkod nga mga tawo; igbabalik ko ha iyo an iyo bugto, ngan makakag-ukoy kamo dinhe ngan makakagpatigayon kamo.’”

en: When they opened their sacks, each man found a pouch of his silver in his sack. When they and their father saw their pouches of silver, they were afraid.
war: Niyan han paghuwara nira han ira mga sako, hin-agian han tagsatagsa ha ira an iya supot hin kwarta; ngan han paghikit-i nira han kwarta, nahadlok hira ngan hi Jacob nga ira amay.

en: Their father Jacob said to them, “You’ve taken my children from me. Joseph’s gone. Simeon’s gone. And you are taking Benjamin. All this can’t really be happening to me!”
war: Nagsiring ha ira an ira tatay, “Karuyag ba niya nga mawara an ngatanan ko nga mga anak? Waray na hi Jose; waray na hi Simeon; ngan yana karuyag niyo kuhaon hi Benjamin. Ako amo an mag-aantos!”

en: The famine was severe in the land,
war: Nagtikagrabi an gutom didto ha Canaan,

en: and when they had eaten all the grain that they brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go back and buy us a little food.”
war: ngan han kaubos na han ngatanan nga trigo nga ira gindara tikang ha Ehipto, nagsiring hi Jacob ha iya mga anak, “Balik kamo ngadto ngan palit hin gutiay nga pagkaon para ha aton.”

en: Judah said to him, “The man was absolutely serious when he said, ‘You may not see me again without your brother with you.’
war: Nagsiring ha iya hi Juda, “Ginpahimatngonan gud kami han tawo nga diri hiya makarawat ha amon kon diri upod namon an amon bugto.

en: If you agree to send our brother with us, then we will go down and buy you food.
war: Kon tumugot ka nga umupod ha amon an amon bugto, makadto kami ngan mapalit hin pagkaon para ha imo.

en: But if you don’t agree to send him, then we can’t go down because the man said to us, ‘You may not see me again without your brother with you.’”
war: Kon diri ka tumugot, diri kami makadto, kay nagsiring ha amon an tawo nga diri gud kami kakarawaton niya gawas kon upod ha amon an amon bugto.”

en: Israel said, “Why have you caused me such pain by telling the man you had another brother?”
war: Nagsiring hi Jacob, “Kay ano hin pagdad-i niyo ha akon hin damo nga kakurian pinaagi hin pagsumat han tawo nga may-ada pa niyo iba nga bugto?”

en: They said, “The man asked us pointedly about our family: ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?’ So we told him just what we’ve said. How were we to know he’d say, ‘Bring your brother down here’?”
war: Nagbaton hira, “Nagpinakiana an tawo hiunong ha aton ngan han aton panimalay, ‘Buhi pa ba an iyo amay? May-ada pa ba kamo iba nga bugto nga lalake?’ Kinahanglan batonon namon an iya mga pakiana. Uunanhon namon hin paghibaro nga iya igpapakuha ha amon an amon bugto?”

en: Judah said to his father Israel, “Send the young man with me. Let’s get ready to leave so that we can stay alive and not die—we, you, and our children.
war: Nagsiring hi Juda ha iya amay, “Paupda ha akon an bata, ngan magkakalakat kami dayon, basi waray ha aton mamamatay hin gutom.

en: I will guarantee his safety; you can hold me responsible. If I don’t bring him back to you and place him here in front of you, it will be my fault forever.
war: Igsasaad ko sugad nga garantiya an akon kalugaringon nga kinabuhi ngan ako an labi nga maaram ha iya. Kon diri ko hiya mahigbalik ha imo ha maupay nga kahimtang, aangkonon ko an kasaypanan ha bug-os ko nga kinabuhi.

en: If we hadn’t waited so long, we would’ve returned twice by now.”
war: Kon waray pa kami paghinulat hin maiha, ngada yana makaduha na unta kami pakabalik.”

en: Their father Israel said to them, “If it has to be, then do this. Take in your bags some of the land’s choice produce, and bring it down to the man as a gift: a little medicinal resin, a little honey, gum, resin, pistachios, and almonds.
war: Nagsiring ha ira an ira amay, “Kon amo man ito an kinahanglan, buhata ini: dad-a ha iyo mga surudlan an gimamag-upayi nga mga abot han tuna sugad nga regalo para han gobernador: mga balsamo, mga dugos, mga pahamot, mga pili, ngan mga almendras.

en: Take twice as much silver with you, and take back the silver returned in the top of your sacks. It might have been a mistake.
war: Pagdara liwat kamo hin duble kadamo nga kwarta, kay kinahanglan igbalik niyo an kwarta nga iginbutang dida ha ganggang han iyo mga sako. Bangin usa la ini nga kalipat.

en: And take your brother, get ready, and go back to the man.
war: Dad-a an iyo bugto, ngan balik kamo dayon.

en: May God Almighty make the man compassionate toward you so that he may send back your other brother and Benjamin with you. But me, if I’m left childless, then I’m left childless.”
war: Igtugot unta han Dyos nga Labi Kamakagarahum nga malooy ha iyo an tawo, basi igbalik ha iyo hin Benjamin ngan an usa pa niyo nga bugto. Para ha akon, kon kinahanglan mawara an akon mga anak, pag-aantoson ko ini.”

en: So the men took this gift. They took twice as much silver with them, together with Benjamin. They left, traveled down to Egypt, and received an audience with Joseph.
war: Sanglit gindara han magburugto an mga regalo ngan duble kadamo nga kwarta, ngan ginmikan hira para ha Ehipto upod hi Benjamin. Didto pinmakita hira kan Jose.

en: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the manager of his household, “Bring the men to the house and slaughter an animal and prepare it because the men will have dinner with me at noon.”
war: Han paghikit-i ni Jose kan Benjamin nga upod ha ira, nagsiring hiya ngadto han surugoon nga tinaporan han iya balay, “Dad-a ini nga mga tawo ngadto han akon balay. Maniningudto hira upod ha akon, sanglit pag-ihaw hin mananap ngan andama ini.”

en: The man did as Joseph told him and brought the men to Joseph’s house.
war: Ginbuhat han surugoon sumala han iginsugo ha iya, ngan gindara an magburugto ngadto han balay ni Jose.

en: When they were brought to Joseph’s house, the men were frightened and said, “We’ve been brought here because of the silver put back in our sacks on our first trip so he can overpower us, capture us, make slaves of us, and take our donkeys.”
war: Samtang gindadara na hira ngadto han balay, nahadlok ngan naghunahuna hira, “Gindadara kita nganhi tungod han kwarta nga iginbutang dida han aton mga sako han syahan ta nga pagkanhi. Aawayon kita nira, kukuhaon an aton mga asno, ngan hihimoon kita nga iya mga oripon.”

en: They approached the man who was Joseph’s household manager and spoke to him at the house’s entrance:
war: Sanglit dida han porta han balay, nagsiring hira ngadto han surugoon nga tinaporan,

en: “Please, Master, we came down the first time just to buy food,
war: “Kon mahimo, mano, kinmanhi kami hadto makausa hin pagpalit hin pagkaon.

en: but when we stopped to spend the night and opened our sacks, there was the exact amount of each man’s silver at the top of his sack. We’ve brought it back with us,
war: Han pagkampo namon dida han amon pagtipauli, gin-abrehan namon an amon mga sako, ngan hin-agian han tagsa ka tawo an iya kwarta dida ha ganggang han iya sako—an ngatanan gud nga kwarta. Amon ini ginbalik nganhi ha imo.

en: and we’ve brought down with us additional silver to buy food. We don’t know who put our silver in our sacks.”
war: Nagdara liwat kami hin darudamo pa nga kwarta nga igpapalit hin dugang nga pagkaon. Diri kami maaram kon hin-o an nag-uli han amon mga kwarta ngadto han amon mga sako.”

en: He said, “You are fine. Don’t be afraid. Your God and your father’s God must have hidden a treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
war: Nagsiring an surugoon, “Ayaw kamo kabaraka. Ayaw kamo kahadlok. Bangin iginbutang han iyo Dyos nga Dyos han iyo amay an kwarta dida han iyo mga sako para ha iyo. Kinmarawat man ako han iyo bayad.” Niyan gindara niya hi Simeon ngada ha ira.

en: The manager brought the men into Joseph’s house and gave them water to wash their feet and feed for their donkeys.
war: Gindara han surugoon an magburugto ngadto han balay. Iya gintagan hira hin tubig basi makagpanhimsaw hira, ngan gintubongan niya an ira mga asno.

en: They prepared the gift, anticipating Joseph’s arrival at noon, since they had heard that they would have a meal there.
war: Gin-andam nira an ira mga regalo nga ighahatag nira kan Jose kon umabot hiya dida han udto, kay ginsumatan man hira nga makikigsaro hiya ha iya.

en: When Joseph came into the house, they presented him the gift they had brought with them into the house, and they bowed low in front of him.
war: Han pag-abot la ni Jose ha balay, gindara nira an regalo ngadto ha iya, ngan nanhapa hira ha iya atubangan.

en: He asked them how they were and said, “How is your elderly father, about whom you spoke? Is he still alive?”
war: Nangumosta hiya ha ira hiunong han ira panlawas ngan katapos nagsiring, “Kumosta man an iyo tatay nga iyo iginsumat ha akon? Buhi pa ba hiya ngan maupay ba an iya panlawas?”

en: They said, “Your servant our father is fine. He’s still alive.” And they bowed down again with deep respect.
war: Binmaton hira, “Buhi pa ngan maupay man gihapon an amon amay nga imo ubos nga surugoon.” Ngan nanluhod ngan nanyukbo hira ha iya atubangan.

en: Joseph looked up and saw his brother Benjamin, his own mother’s son, and he said, “Is this your youngest brother whom you told me about? God be gracious to you, my son.”
war: Han paghikit-i la ni Jose kan Benjamin nga iya bugto, nagsiring hiya, “O, amo ngay-an ini an iyo gimamanghori nga bugto nga iginsumat niyo ha akon. Pagbendisyonan ka unta han Dyos, anak ko.”

en: Joseph’s feelings for his brother were so strong he was about to weep, so he rushed to another room and wept there.
war: Niyan binmaya hi Jose hin kadagmitan kay tugob na gud an iya kasingkasing hin kalooy para han iya bugto. Nag-iitarangis na hiya, sanglit sinmulod hiya han iya kwarto ngan nagtangis.

en: He washed his face, came back, pulled himself together, and said, “Set out the dinner.”
war: Katapos niya maghiramos, ginmawas hiya nga ginpupugngan niya an iya kalugaringon ngan nagsugo hiya nga magdurot na han pagkaon.

en: So they set out his food by himself, their food by themselves, and the Egyptians’ who ate with him by themselves because Egyptians don’t allow themselves to eat with Hebrews; the Egyptians think it beneath their dignity.
war: Gindurotan hi Jose dida hin usa nga lamesa ngan ha lain nga lamesa an iya kabugtoan. Gindurotan didto hin lain nga lamesa an mga Ehiptohanon nga nangangaon didto, kay ha ira paghunahuna makakapahiubos gud ha ira an pakigsaro han mga Hebreo.

en: They were seated in front of him from the oldest to the youngest in their exact birth order, and the men looked at each other with amazement.
war: Ginpalingkod an kabugtoan nga naatubang kan Jose hin sunodsunod sumala han ira panuigon, tikang han gimamagurangi ngadto han gimamanghori. Han paghikit-i nira han ira sunodsunod nga pangalingkod, naggipasirusiplat hira hin paghipausa.

en: Portions of food from Joseph’s table were brought to them, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as large as theirs. So they drank together and were at ease.
war: Gindurotan hira hin pagkaon tikang didto han lamesa ni Jose, ngan gindurotan hi Benjamin hin lima ka pilo kadamo kay han igindurot han iba ha ira. Sanglit nangaon ngan nag-irignom hira upod kan Jose tubtob han pagkahuhubog nira.

en: Joseph gave commands to his household manager: “Fill the men’s sacks with as much food as they’ll hold, and put each man’s silver at the top of his sack.
war: Ginsugo ni Jose an surugoon nga tinaporan han iya balay, “Pun-a hin trigo an mga sako han mga tawo tubtob han ira maaakos hin pagdara, ngan igsulod ha ganggang han iya sako an kwarta han kada tawo.

en: Put my cup, the silver cup, on top of the youngest brother’s sack, together with the silver for his grain.” So he did just as Joseph told him to do.
war: Igsulod ha ganggang han sako han gimamanghori nga bugto an akon kupa nga salapi upod han kwarta nga palit han iya trigo.” Gintuman niya sumala han iginsugo ha iya.

en: At dawn, the men and their donkeys were sent off.
war: Timprano pa han pagkaaga, ginpalakat an magburugto dara an ira mga asno.

en: They had left the city but hadn’t gone far when Joseph said to his household manager, “Get ready, go after the men and catch up with them! Ask them, ‘Why have you repaid hospitality with ingratitude?
war: Han diri pa hira hirayo tikang han syudad, ginsiring ni Jose an iya surugoon nga tinaporan han iya balay, “Dali ngan lanata an mga tawo. Kon hiabotan mo hira pakianhi hira, ‘Kay ano nga ginbalos man niyo hin maraot an maupay?

en: Isn’t this the cup my master drinks from and uses to discover God’s plans? What you’ve done is despicable.’”
war: Kay ano nga ginkawat niyo an kupa nga salapi han akon agaron? Amo ini an kupa nga iniimnan niya, an kupa nga ginagamit niya hin pagtagna han tiarabot nga panahon. Ginbuhat niyo in dako gud nga sala!’”

en: When he caught up to them, he repeated these words.
war: Han paghiabti ha ira han surugoon, iginyakan niya ha ira ini ngahaw nga mga pulong.

en: They replied, “Why does my master talk to us like this? Your servants would never do such a thing.
war: Ira ginbaton hiya, “Ano an karuyag mo sidngon, mano, hin pagyakan mo hin sugad hini? Nagsusumpa kami nga waray gud namon pagbuhata in sugad nga butang.

en: The silver that we found at the top of our sacks, we’ve just brought back to you from the land of Canaan. We didn’t steal silver or gold from your master’s house.
war: Maaram ka man nga iginbalik ngani namon ha imo tikang ha tuna han Canaan an kwarta nga amon hin-agian dida han ganggang han amon mga sako. Kay ano nga mangangawat kami hin salapi o bulawan tikang han balay han imo agaron?

en: Whoever of your servants is found with it will be put to death, and we’ll be my master’s slaves.”
war: Kon hiagian in usa ha amon nga may-ada hini nga kupa, kinahanglan pagpatayon hiya, ngan magigin mga oripon nimo kami ngatanan.”

en: He said, “Fine. We’ll do just as you’ve said. Whoever is found with it will be my slave, and the rest of you will go free.”
war: Nagsiring hiya, “Nauyon ako; kundi hiya la nga nakadara han kupa an magigin akon oripon, ngan mahigagawas-kamo ngatanan han kataragman.”

en: Everyone quickly lowered their sacks down to the ground and each opened his sack.
war: Sanglit ginhaw-as dayon nira ha tuna an ira mga sako, ngan ginbukas an sako han kada tawo.

en: He searched the oldest first and the youngest last, and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
war: Gin-usisa hin maupay han surugoon ni Jose tikang han gimamagurangi ngadto han gimamanghori, ngan hin-agian an kupa didto han sako ni Benjamin.

en: At this, they tore their clothing. Then everyone loaded their donkeys, and they returned to the city.
war: Ginggisi han magburugto an ira mga panapton tungod hin kabidoan, iginkargahan han mga asno an ira mga sako, ngan binmalik hira ngadto han syudad.

en: When Judah and his brothers arrived at Joseph’s house, he was still there, and they fell to the ground in front of him.
war: Han pag-abot nira Juda ngan han iya kabugtoan ngadto han balay ni Jose, nakadto pa hiya. Nanyukbo hira ha atubangan niya,

en: Joseph said to them, “What’s this you’ve done? Didn’t you know someone like me can discover God’s plans?”
war: ngan nagsiring hi Jose, “Ano an iyo ginbuhat? Diri ba kamo maaram nga mahibabaroan an iyo ginbubuhat hin usa ka tawo nga sugad ha akon, pinaagi hin pagtag-na?”

en: Judah replied, “What can we say to my master? What words can we use? How can we prove we are innocent? God has found your servants guilty. We are now your slaves, all of us, including the one found with the cup.”
war: “Ano man an amon igsisiring ha imo, ginoo?” binmaton hi Juda. “Uunanhon namon hin pakagdiwara? Uunanhon namon hin pakagpahayag nga waray kami kasal-anan? Ginpahayag han Dyos an amon sala. Yana mga oripon na nimo kami ngatanan, diri la hiya kan kanay hin-agian an kupa.”

en: Joseph said, “I’d never do such a thing. Only the man found with the cup will be my slave. As for the rest of you, you are free to go back to your father.”
war: Nagsiring hi Jose, “Diri! Diri gud ako magbubuhat hito! Hiya la nga hin-agian ha iya an kupa an magigin akon oripon. Makakauli na an iba ha iyo ngadto han iyo amay; waray gud malalabot ha iyo.”

en: Judah approached him and said, “Please, my master, allow your servant to say something to my master without getting angry with your servant since you are like Pharaoh himself.
war: Dinmaop hi Juda kan Jose ngan nagsiring, “Ginoo, tugoti gad ako hin pakighimangraw ha imo. Ayaw intawon ako kasinahi; sugad ka han hadi ngahaw namon.

en: My master asked his servants, ‘Do you have a father or brother?’
war: Ginpakianhan mo kami, ‘May-ada ba niyo amay, o lain nga bugto nga lalake?’

en: And we said to my master, ‘Yes, we have an elderly father and a young brother, born when he was old. His brother is dead and he’s his mother’s only child. But his father loves him.’
war: Binmaton kami, ‘May-ada pa kami amay nga lagas na ngan hin usa nga manghud nga lalake, nga anak niya dida han lagas na hiya. Patay na an bugto hini nga bata, ngan hiya na la an buhi pa nga anak han iroy niya: hinigugma hiya hin duro han amon amay.’

en: You told your servants, ‘Bring him down to me so I can see him.’
war: Ginsiring mo kami hin pagdara ha iya nganhi basi makakita ka ha iya,

en: And we said to my master, ‘The young man can’t leave his father. If he leaves, his father will die.’
war: ngan binmaton kami nga diri makakabaya han iya amay an bata; kon buhaton niya ini mapatay an iya amay.

en: You said to your servants, ‘If your youngest brother doesn’t come down with you, you’ll never see my face again.’
war: Niyan nagsiring ka, ‘Diri kamo kakarawaton ha akon atubangan gawas kon umupod ha iyo an iyo gimamanghori nga bugto.’

en: “When we went back to my father your servant, we told him what you said.
war: “Han pagbalik namon ngadto han amon amay, amon hiya ginsumatan han imo iginsiring.

en: Our father told us, ‘Go back and buy for us a little food.’
war: Niyan ginpabalik kami niya ngan ginpapalit hin pagkaon.

en: But we said, ‘We can’t go down. We will go down only if our youngest brother is with us. We won’t be able to gain an audience with the man without our youngest brother with us.’
war: Binmaton kami, ‘Diri kami makakakadto; diri kami kakarawaton han tawo gawas kon upod namon an amon gimamanghori nga bugto. Makadto la kami kon bunyog namon an amon gimamanghori nga bugto.’

en: Your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife gave birth to two sons for me.
war: Nagsiring ha amon an amon amay, ‘Maaram man kamo nga duha la nga mga anak nga lalake an igin-anak namon ngan hi Raquel nga akon asawa.

en: One disappeared and I said, “He must have been torn up by a wild animal,” and I haven’t seen him since.
war: Binayaan na ako han usa ha ira. Bangin ginpikaspikas hiya hin magpintas nga mga mananap, kay waray ko na man hiya hikit-i tikang hiya lumakat.

en: And if you take this one from me too, something terrible will happen to him, and you will send me—old as I am—to my grave in despair.’
war: Kon kuhaon niyo ini nga usa tikang ha akon yana, ngan may-ada mahinabo ha iya makakamatay ha akon an kabidoan nga iyo bubuhaton ha akon kay lagas na ako.’”

en: When I now go back to your servant my father without the young man—whose life is so bound up with his—
war: 30-31 “Ngan yana, ginoo,” nagpadayon hi Juda, “kon bumalik ako ngadto han akon amay nga waray an bata, ha pagkita gudla niya nga diri ko upod an bata, mapatay manta hiya. Mag-usa la an kinabuhi han bata ngan han iya kinabuhi. Makakapabido kami han amon amay ngan amo an makakamatay ha iya, kay lagas na hiya hin duro.

en: and when he sees that the young man isn’t with us, he will die, and your servants will have sent our father your servant—old as he is—to his grave in grief.
war: Labot pa hini iginsaad ko han akon amay an akon kinabuhi sugad nga garantiya han bata. Ginsiring ko hiya nga kon diri ko igbalik ha iya an bata, pag-aangkonon ko an sayop ha bug-os ko nga kinabuhi.

en: I, your servant, guaranteed the young man’s safety to my father, telling him, ‘If I don’t bring him back to you, it will be my fault forever.’
war: Ngan yana, ginoo, magpapabilin ako dinhe sugad nga imo oripon saliwan han bata; pabalika hiya upod han iya kabugtoan.

en: Now, please let your servant stay as your slave instead of the young man so that he can go back with his brothers.
war: Uunanhon ko hin pakabalik ngadto han akon amay kon diri ko upod an bata? Diri ako mailob hin pagkita hini nga karat-an nga maabot han akon tatay.”

en: Joseph could no longer control himself in front of all his attendants, so he declared, “Everyone, leave now!” So no one stayed with him when he revealed his identity to his brothers.
war: Waray na pakakapugong hi Jose han iya mga pagbati ha atubangan han iya mga surugoon, sanglit iya ginsugo hira ngatanan hin pagbaya han kwarto. Waray na iba nga kaupod niya han pagpakilala ni Jose ngadto han iya kabugtoan.

en: He wept so loudly that the Egyptians and Pharaoh’s household heard him.
war: Nagtangis hiya upod in makusog nga mga pagbakho nga hinbatian hiya han mga Ehiptohanon, ngan gindara an sumat ngadto han palasyo han hadi.

en: Joseph said to his brothers, “I’m Joseph! Is my father really still alive?” His brothers couldn’t respond because they were terrified before him.
war: Nagsiring hi Jose ngadto han iya kabugtoan, “Amo ako hi Jose. Buhi pa ba an akon amay?” Kundi han pakabati hini han iya kabugtoan, nahadlok hira hin duro nga waray hira pakabaton.

en: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come closer to me,” and they moved closer. He said, “I’m your brother Joseph! The one you sold to Egypt.
war: Niyan nagsiring ha ira hi Jose, “Alayon duok kamo ngadi.” Dinmuok hira ngan nagsiring hiya, “Amo ako hi Jose nga iyo bugto nga iginbaligya niyo nganhi ha Ehipto.

en: Now, don’t be upset and don’t be angry with yourselves that you sold me here. Actually, God sent me before you to save lives.
war: Yana ayaw kamo kabaraka o pagbasol ha iyo ngahaw tungod nga iginbaligya ako niyo nganhi. An Dyos amo gud an nagpadara ha akon hin pag-una ha iyo nganhi hin pagtalwas han mga kinabuhi hin mga tawo.

en: We’ve already had two years of famine in the land, and there are five years left without planting or harvesting.
war: Ikaduha pala ka tuig ini nga gutom dinhe ha tuna; may-ada lilima pa ka tuig nga mawawaray pag-arado o pag-ani.

en: God sent me before you to make sure you’d survive and to rescue your lives in this amazing way.
war: Ginpauna ako ha iyo han Dyos hin pagtalwas ha iyo ha sugad hini nga urosahon nga paagi ngan pagsiguro nga mabuhi kamo ngan an iyo mga tulin.

en: You didn’t send me here; it was God who made me a father to Pharaoh, master of his entire household, and ruler of the whole land of Egypt.
war: Sanglit diri gud kamo kundi an Dyos amo an nagpadara ha akon nganhi. Ginhimo ako niya nga gilalabawi nga opisyal han hadi. Amo ako an tinaporan han iya bug-os nga nasod; amo ako an punoan han bug-os nga Ehipto.”

en: “Hurry! Go back to your father. Tell him this is what your son Joseph says: ‘God has made me master of all of Egypt. Come down to me. Don’t delay.
war: “Yana pagdagmit kamo hin pagbalik ngadto han akon tatay ngan sumati hiya nga amo ini an siring ni Jose nga iya anak, ‘Ginhimo ako han Dyos nga punoan han bug-os nga Ehipto; pakadi ha akon hin waray paglangan.

en: You may live in the land of Goshen, so you will be near me, your children, your grandchildren, your flocks, your herds, and everyone with you.
war: Makakag-ukoy ka didto han katunaan han Gosen diin mahihirani kamo ha akon—ikaw, an imo mga anak, an imo mga apo, an imo mga karnero, an imo mga kanding, an imo mga baka, ngan an ngatanan nga iba pa nga imo mga hiagi.

en: I will support you there, so you, your household, and everyone with you won’t starve, since the famine will still last five years.’
war: Kon aadto ka na ha Gosen, makakagmangno ako ha iyo. May lilima pa ka tuig nga gutom; ngan diri ko karuyag nga panggutomon ikaw, an imo panimalay, ngan an imo mga hayop.’”

en: You and my brother Benjamin have seen with your own eyes that I’m speaking to you.
war: Nagpadayon hi Jose, “Yana nakakakita kamo ngatanan, ngan ikaw liwat Benjamin nga amo gud ako hi Jose.

en: Tell my father about my power in Egypt and about everything you’ve seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.”
war: Sumati an akon tatay nga gamhanan na ako dinhe ha Ehipto ngan sumati hiya hiunong han ngatanan nga iyo hinkit-an. Niyan pagdagmit kamo ngan dad-a hiya nganhi.”

en: He threw his arms around his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his shoulder.
war: Ginhangkopan niya hi Benjamin nga iya bugto ngan nagtangis hira nga duha; nagtangis liwat hi Benjamin samtang ginggagakos niya hi Jose.

en: He kissed all of his brothers and wept, embracing them. After that, his brothers were finally able to talk to him.
war: Ngan samtang nagtitinangis pa hi Jose, ginhangkopan niya an kada usa han iya kabugtoan ngan ginhagkan hira. Katapos hito, nakighimangraw na ha iya an iya kabugtoan.

en: When Pharaoh’s household heard the message “Joseph’s brothers have arrived,” both Pharaoh and his servants were pleased.
war: Han pag-abot han sumat ngadto ha palasyo nga nagkaabot an kabugtoan ni Jose, nalipay an hadi ngan an iya mga opisyal.

en: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Give your brothers these instructions: Load your pack animals and go back to the land of Canaan.
war: Nagsiring an hadi kan Jose, “Sidnga an imo kabugtoan nga kargahan an ira mga hayop ngan bumalik hira ngadto han tuna han Canaan.

en: Get your father and your households and come back to me. Let me provide you with good things from the land of Egypt so that you may eat the land’s best food.
war: Ipakuha ha ira an ira amay ngan an ira mga panimalay, ngan pabalika hira nganhi. Ighahatag ko ha ira an gimamaupayi nga tuna dinhe ha Ehipto, ngan mahuhura hira hin pagkaon.

en: Give them these instructions too: Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your children and wives, and pick up your father and come back.
war: Ipadara liwat ha ira in mga karomata tikang ha Ehipto, para han ira kaasaw-an ngan han ira gudtiay nga kabataan, ngan paupda ha ira an ira amay.

en: Don’t worry about your possessions because you will have good things from the entire land of Egypt.”
war: Diri hira angay mabaraka hin pagbaya han ira mga butang; magtatag-iya hira han gimamaupayi dinhe han bug-os nga tuna han Ehipto.”

en: So Israel’s sons did that. Joseph gave them wagons as Pharaoh instructed, and he gave them provisions for the road.
war: Gintuman han mga anak ni Jacob sumala han iginsiring ha ira. Gintagan hira ni Jose hin mga karomata ngan pagkaon para han ira paglalaktan sumala han iginsugo han hadi.

en: To all of them he gave a change of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
war: Gintagan liwat niya hin liliwanan nga panapton an kada usa ha ira, kundi gintagan niya hi Benjamin hin tulo ka gatos ka bug-os nga salapi ngan lima nga liliwanan nga mga panapton.

en: To his father he sent ten male donkeys carrying goods from Egypt, ten female donkeys carrying grain and bread, and rations for his father for the road.
war: Ginpadad-an niya an iya amay hin napulo nga mga asno nga kargado han labi kamaupay, nga mga butang ha Ehipto, ngan napulo nga mga asno nga kargado hin mga liniso, tinapay, ngan iba pa nga pagkaon para han ira paglalaktan.

en: He sent his brothers off; and as they were leaving, he told them, “Don’t be worried about the trip.”
war: Ginpagikan niya an iya kabugtoan ngan han nalakat na hira, gintugon niya hira, “Ayaw kamo pag-aruaraway dida han dalan.”

en: So they left Egypt and returned to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.
war: Ginmawas hira han Ehipto ngan nangoli hira ngadto kan Jacob nga ira amay didto ha Canaan.

en: They announced to him, “Joseph’s still alive! He’s actually ruler of all the land of Egypt!” Jacob’s heart nearly failed, and he didn’t believe them.
war: Ira ginsumatan hiya, “Buhi pa hi Jose! Amo hiya an punoan han bug-os nga Ehipto!” Nahitingala hi Jacob, ngan waray gud hiya anay tutuod ha ira.

en: When they told him everything Joseph had said to them, and when he saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, Jacob recovered.
war: Kundi han ira nagpagsumati ha iya han ngatanan nga iginsiring ha ira ni Jose, ngan han paghikit-i niya han mga karomata nga iginpadara ni Jose para hin pagdara ha iya ngadto ha Ehipto, nawara an iya paghitingala ngan nalipay hiya.

en: Then Israel said, “This is too much! My son Joseph is still alive! Let me go and see him before I die.”
war: Nagsiring hiya, “Buhi pa hi Jose nga akon anak! Amo la ini an akon pinangangaro. Kinahanglan kumadto ako ngan hikit-an ko hiya san-o ako mamatay.”

en: Israel packed up everything he owned and traveled to Beer-sheba. There he offered sacrifices to his father Isaac’s God.
war: Namutos ni Jacob han ngatanan nga iya mga hiagi ngan kinmadto hiya ha Berseba, diin naghalad hiya hin mga halad nga tinubod ngadto han Dyos ni Isaac nga iya amay.

en: God said to Israel in a vision at night, “Jacob! Jacob!” and he said, “I’m here.”
war: Naghimangraw ha iya an Dyos dida hin usa nga panan-awon ha gab-i ngan nagtawag, “Jacob, Jacob!”

en: He said, “I am El, your father’s God. Don’t be afraid to go down to Egypt because I will make a great nation of you there.
war: Binmaton hiya, “Oo, aadi ako.”

en: I will go down to Egypt with you, and I promise to bring you out again. Joseph will close your eyes when you die.”
war: “Amo ako an Dyos nga Dyos han imo amay,” nagsiring an Dyos. “Ayaw kahadlok hin pagkadto ha Ehipto; didto hihimoon ko nga dako nga nasod an imo mga tulin.

en: Then Jacob left Beer-sheba. Israel’s sons put their father Jacob, their children, and their wives on the wagons Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
war: Maupod ako ha imo ngadto ha Ehipto ngan igbabalik ko an imo mga tulin nganhi hini nga tuna. Aada ha imo kagiliran hi Jose kon mamatay ka.”

en: They took their livestock and their possessions that they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and arrived in Egypt, Jacob and all of his children with him.
war: Ginmikan hi Jacob tikang ha Berseba. Ginpasakay han iya mga anak hiya, an ira kabataan, ngan an ira kaasaw-an dida han mga karomata nga ginpadara han hadi han Ehipto.

en: His sons and grandsons, his daughters and his granddaughters—all of his descendants he brought with him to Egypt.
war: Gindara nira an ira mga hayop ngan an mga hiagi nga naangkon nira didto ha Canaan, ngan kinmadto hira ha Ehipto. Ginpaupod ni Jacob an ngatanan niya nga mga tulin:

en: These are the names of the Israelites who went to Egypt, including Jacob and his sons. Jacob’s oldest son was Reuben.
war: an iya mga anak nga kalalaken-an ngan mga apo nga kalalaken-an, ngan an iya mga anak nga kababayen-an ngan mga apo nga kababayen-an.

en: Reuben’s sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
war: Amo ini an mga kaapi han panimalay ni Jacob nga inmupod ha iya ngadto ha Ehipto: an gimamagurangi nga anak ni Jacob nga hi Ruben,

en: Simeon’s sons were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, whose mother was a Canaanite.
war: ngan an mga anak nga kalalaken-an ni Ruben: hira Hanoc, Falu, Hesron, ug Carmi.

en: Levi’s sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
war: Hi Simeon ngan an iya mga anak: hira Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jaquin, Zohar, ug Saul nga anak hin babaye nga Canaanhon.

en: Judah’s sons were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. Er and Onan both died in the land of Canaan. Perez’s sons were Hezron and Hamul.
war: Hi Levi ngan an iya mga anak: hira Gerson, Coat, ug Merari.

en: Issachar’s sons were Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.
war: Hi Juda ngan an iya mga anak: hira Sela, Peres, ug Sera (namatay didto ha Canaan an iba nga mga anak ni Juda nga hira Er ug Onan). Hira Hesron ug Hamul nga mga anak ni Peres.

en: Zebulun’s sons were Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
war: Hi Isacar ngan an iya mga anak: hira Tola, Pua, Jasub, ug Simron.

en: These are the sons Leah bore to Jacob in Paddan-aram. Her daughter was Dinah. All of these persons, including his sons and daughters, totaled 33.
war: Hi Zabulon ngan an iya mga anak: hira Sered, Elon, ug Jaleel.

en: Gad’s sons were Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
war: Amo ini an mga anak nga kalalaken-an nga igin-anak nira Lea ug Jacob didto ha Mesopotamia, labot kan Dina nga iya anak nga babaye. Naabot hin 33 ngatanan nga mga tulin nira Jacob ug Lea.

en: Asher’s sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah. Beriah’s sons were Heber and Malchiel.
war: Hi Gad ngan an iya mga anak: hira Sifeon, Hagi, Suni, Ezbon, Eri, Arod, ug Areli.

en: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Leah. She bore these to Jacob, a total of 16 persons.
war: Hi Aser ngan an iya mga anak: hira Jimna, Isva, Isvi, Beria, ug hi Sera nga ira bugto nga babaye. Hira Heber ug Malkiel nga mga anak ni Beria.

en: The sons of Jacob’s wife Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.
war: Amo ini nga 16 an mga tulin nira Jacob ug Zilpa nga oripon nga babaye nga iginhatag ni Laban kan Lea nga iya anak.

en: To Joseph, in the land of Egypt, were born Manasseh and Ephraim. Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore them to him.
war: Nag-anak hira Raquel ug Jacob hin duha nga lalake: hira Jose ug Benjamin.

en: Benjamin’s sons were Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
war: May duha nga mga anak nga kalalaken-an hi Jose didto ha Ehipto: hira Manases ug Efraim, pinaagi kan Asenat nga anak ni Potifera nga padi didto ha Heliopolis.

en: These are Rachel’s sons who were born to Jacob, a total of 14 persons.
war: Hira Bela, Bequer, Asbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Ros, Mupim, Hupim, ug Ard nga mga anak ni Benjamin.

en: Dan’s son was Hushim.
war: Amo ini nga 14 an mga tulin nira Jacob ug Raquel.

en: Naphtali’s sons were Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
war: Hi Dan ngan hi Husim nga iya anak.

en: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel. She bore these to Jacob, a total of 7 persons.
war: Hi Neftali ngan an iya mga anak: hira Jazeel, Guni, Jezer, ug Silem.

en: All of the persons going to Egypt with Jacob—his own children, excluding Jacob’s sons’ wives—totaled 66 persons.
war: Amo ini nga pito an mga tulin nira Jacob ug Bilha nga oripon nga babaye nga iginhatag ni Laban kan Raquel nga iya anak.

en: Joseph’s sons born to him in Egypt were 2 persons. Thus, all of the persons in Jacob’s household going to Egypt totaled 70.
war: Sesenta y seis ka tawo ngatanan an mga tulin ni Jacob nga kinmadto ha Ehipto, waray labot han kaasaw-an han iya mga anak.

en: Israel had sent Judah ahead to Joseph so that Joseph could explain the way to Goshen. Then they arrived in the land of Goshen.
war: Natawo kan Jose didto ha Ehipto in duha nga mga anak nga kalalaken-an, ngan naabot hin 70 ka tawo ngatanan han panimalay ni Jacob an kinmadto ha Ehipto.

en: Joseph hitched up his chariot and went to meet his father Israel in Goshen. When he arrived, he threw his arms around his neck and wept, embracing him for a long time.
war: Ginpauna ni Jacob hi Juda hin paghangyo kan Jose nga tapoon hira didto ha Gosen. Han pag-abot la nira,

en: Israel said to Joseph, “I can die now after seeing your face. You are really still alive!”
war: sinmakay hi Jose han iya karwahe ngan kinmadto ha Gosen hin pagtapo han iya tatay. Han pagkatapo nira, hinangkopan ni Jose an iya tatay ngan nagtinangis hiya hin maiha.

en: Joseph said to his brothers and to his father’s household, “Let me go up and inform Pharaoh and tell him, ‘My brothers and my father’s household who were in the land of Canaan have arrived.
war: Nagsiring hi Jacob kan Jose, “Andam na ako hin kamatay, yana nga hinkit-an ko na ikaw ngan maaram na ako nga buhi ka pa ngay-an.”

en: The men are shepherds, because they own livestock. They’ve brought with them their flocks and herds and everything they own.’
war: Niyan nagsiring hi Jose ha iya kabugtoan ngan ha iba nga mga kaapi han panimalay han iya amay, “Kinahanglan kumadto ako ngan pagsumatan ko an hadi nga inmabot na ha akon an akon kabugtoan ngan an ngatanan nga mga kaapi han panimalay han akon amay nga nag-ukoy didto ha Canaan.

en: When Pharaoh summons you and says, ‘What do you do?’
war: Susumatan ko hiya nga mga magmarangno kamo hin mga karnero ngan nagmamangno kamo hin mga hayop, ngan iyo gindara an iyo mga panon hin mga karnero ngan mga baka ngan an ngatanan nga mga hiagi ug manggad.

en: say, ‘Your servants have owned livestock since we were young, both we and our ancestors,’ so that you will be able to settle in the land of Goshen, since Egyptians think all shepherds are beneath their dignity.”
war: Kon tawgon kamo han hadi ngan magpakiana kon ano an iyo pagpakabuhi,

en: Joseph went to inform Pharaoh and said, “My father and brothers with their flocks, herds, and everything they own have come from the land of Canaan and are now in the land of Goshen.”
war: Sanglit gindara ni Jose in lima han iya kabugtoan ngan kinmadto hira han hadi. Ginsumatan niya an hadi, “Kinmanhi na tikang ha Canaan an akon amay ngan an akon kabugtoan upod an ira mga panon hin mga kakarnero, an ira mga baka, ngan an hiagi ug manggad. Aadto na hira yana ha katunaan han Gosen.”

en: From all of his brothers, he selected five men and presented them before Pharaoh.
war: Niyan iginpakilala niya han hadi an iya kabugtoan.

en: Pharaoh said to Joseph’s brothers, “What do you do?”
war: Ginpakianhan hira han hadi, “Ano an iyo pakabuhi?”

en: They said to Pharaoh, “Your servants are shepherds, both we and our ancestors.”
war: Binmaton hira, “Magmarangno kami hin kahayopan, sugad han amon kaapoy-apoyan.

en: They continued, “We’ve come to the land as immigrants because the famine is so severe in the land of Canaan that there are no more pastures for your servants’ flocks. Please allow your servants to settle in the land of Goshen.”
war: Kinmanhi kami hin pag-ukoy dinhe hini nga nasod, kay makalilisang an gutom didto ha tuna han Canaan nga waray na panabsaban para han amon mga panon. Tugoti gad kami hin pag-ukoy didto han katunaan han Gosen.”

en: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since your father and brothers have arrived,
war: Nagsiring an hadi kan Jose, “Yana nga nagkaabot na an imo amay ngan an imo kabugtoan,

en: the land of Egypt is available to you. Settle your father and brothers in the land’s best location. Let them live in the land of Goshen. And if you know capable men among them, put them in charge of my own livestock.”
war: ira an tuna han Ehipto. Paukya hira didto han katunaan han Gosen, an labi hin kamaupay nga bahin han tuna. Ngan kon may-ada ha ira may katakos nga mga tawo, igbutang hira nga tinaporan han akon kalugaringon nga mga hayop.”

en: Joseph brought his father Jacob and gave him an audience with Pharaoh. Jacob blessed Pharaoh,
war: Niyan gindara ni Jose hi Jacob nga iya amay ngan iginpakilala hiya han hadi. Ginbendisyonan ni Jacob an hadi,

en: and Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How old are you?”
war: ngan ginpakianhan hiya han hadi, “Pira na an imo panuigon?”

en: Jacob said to Pharaoh, “I’ve been a traveler for 130 years. My years have been few and difficult. They don’t come close to the years my ancestors lived during their travels.”
war: Binmaton hi Jacob, “Inmabot na hin 130 ka tuig an akon kinabuhi hin paglakaton. Halipotay ngan magkuri ito nga mga tuig, diri sugad han halawig nga kinabuhi han akon mga ginikanan dida han ira mga paglakaton.”

en: Jacob blessed Pharaoh and left Pharaoh’s presence.
war: Ginbendisyonan ni Jacob hin panamilit an hadi, ngan linmakat hiya.

en: Joseph settled his father and brothers and gave them property in the land of Egypt, in the best location in the land of Rameses, just as Pharaoh had ordered.
war: Ngan iginpahimutang ni Jose didto ha Ehipto an iya amay ngan an iya kabugtoan ngan tinagan hira hin mga hiagi didto han labi hin kamaupay nga bahin han tuna nga hirani han syudad han Rameses, sumala han iginsugo han hadi.

en: Joseph provided food for his father, his brothers, and his father’s entire household, in proportion to the number of children.
war: Naghatag hi Jose hin pagkaon para han iya amay, han iya kabugtoan, ngan han ngatanan nga sakop han panimalay han iya amay, lakip an mga kabataan.

en: There was no food in the land because the famine was so severe. The land of Egypt and the land of Canaan dried up from the famine.
war: Grabe na hin duro an gutom nga waray na gud pagkaon bisan diin ngan nagtikaluya na tungod hin kagutom an mga tawo han Ehipto ug Canaan.

en: Joseph collected all of the silver to be found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan for the grain, which people came to buy, and he deposited it in Pharaoh’s treasury.
war: Samtang namamalit an mga tawo hin liniso, gintirok ni Jose an ngatanan nga kwarta ngan gindara ini niya ngadto han palasyo.

en: The silver from the land of Egypt and from the land of Canaan had been spent, and all of the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, “Give us food. Why should we die before your eyes, just because the silver is gone?”
war: Han kaubos na han ngatanan nga kwarta didto ha Ehipto ug Canaan, kinmadto kan Jose an mga Ehiptohanon ngan nagsiring, “Tagi kami hin pagkaon! Ayaw gad itugot nga magkamatay kami. Buhata na an sadang nimo mahimo! Waray na kami kwarta.”

en: Joseph said, “Give me your livestock, and I will give you food for your livestock if the silver is gone.”
war: Binmaton hi Jose, “Dad-a an iyo mga baka; babalyoon ko ini hin pagkaon kon waray na niyo kwarta.”

en: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them food for the horses, flocks, cattle, and donkeys. He got them through that year with food in exchange for all of their livestock.
war: Sanglit gindara nira an ira mga hayop ngadto kan Jose, ngan iya gintagan hira hin pagkaon nga balyo han ira mga kabayo, mga karnero, mga kanding, mga baka, ngan mga asno. Hito nga tuig iya gintagan hira hin pagkaon nga balyo han ngatanan nira nga mga hayop.

en: When that year was over, they came to him the next year and said to him, “We can’t hide from my master that the silver is spent and that we’ve given the livestock to my master. All that’s left for my master is our corpses and our farmland.
war: Han pagkasunod nga tuig kinmadto hira kan Jose ngan nagsiring, “Magsusumat kami han kamatuoran nga waray nagud kami kwarta ngan aada na ha imo an amon mga hayop. Waray na gud nahibilin nga sadang ighatag namon ha imo labot han amon mga lawas ngan han amon mga tuna.

en: Why should we die before your eyes, we and our farmland too? Buy us and our farms for food, and we and our farms will be under Pharaoh’s control. Give us seed so that we can stay alive and not die, and so that our farmland won’t become unproductive.”
war: Ayaw gad itugot nga magkamatay kami. Buhata an sadang nimo mahimo. Ayaw gad itugot nga mahimo nga kamingawan an amon kaumhan. Palita kami ngan an amon tuna nga balyo hin pagkaon. Himoa kami nga mga oripon han hadi ngan ihahatag namon ha iya an amon tuna. Tagi kami hin trigo basi mabuhi kami, ngan hin binhe basi makagtanom kami han amon kaumhan.”

en: So Joseph bought all of Egypt’s farmland for Pharaoh because every Egyptian sold his field when the famine worsened. So the land became Pharaoh’s.
war: Ginpalit ni Jose para han hadi an ngatanan nga tuna didto ha Ehipto. Napirit hin pagbaligya han ira tuna an ngatanan nga mga Ehiptohanon kay grabe na hin duro an gutom; sanglit natag-iya na han hadi an ngatanan nga katunaan.

en: He moved the people to the cities from one end of Egypt to the other.
war: Ginhimo ni Jose nga mga oripon an mga tawo tikang ha usa ngadto ha luyo nga kataposan han Ehipto.

en: However, he didn’t buy the farmland of the priests because Pharaoh allowed the priests a subsidy, and they were able to eat from the subsidy Pharaoh gave them. Therefore, they didn’t have to sell their farmland.
war: An tuna la nga gintatag-iya han kapadian an waray niya pagpalita. Waray na nira kinahanglan hin pagbaligya han ira mga tuna, kay gintagan man hira han hadi hin bahin nga sadang nira kabuhian.

en: Joseph said to the people, “Since I’ve now purchased you and your farmland for Pharaoh, here’s seed for you. Plant the seed on the land.
war: Nagsiring hi Jose ha mga tawo, “Hinkit-an niyo nga ginpalit ko na kamo ngan an iyo mga tuna para han hadi. Iini in binhe para hin pagpugas didto han iyo kaumhan.

en: When the crop comes in, you must give one-fifth to Pharaoh. You may keep four-fifths for yourselves, for planting fields, and for feeding yourselves, those in your households, and your children.”
